A fun RTS. The difficulty is very accessible even for those not familiar with the genre.

The base game loop is exactly what you’d expect from an RTS: You build an economic workforce, you build a military, you gather resources and fight enemies. That’s not where this game shines.

What makes this game for me is how the dev managed to nudge you into building what looks like a realistic ant nest: There’s bonuses to be had for building separate chambers for separate concerns, there’s a malus for building everything in the way.

The notifications is also very much to my liking. Instead of a fanfare or a ‘the enemy is attacking’ call when … well the enemy is attacking, you get a BBC narrator explaining “The ants are under attack. They must protect the larvae.“ A very nice execution of a base necessity.

Even the way the ants move makes it look very much like a buzzing ant hive.

There are some minor issues I would’ve liked addressed, but they’re not terrible:

- Ants move randomly around their assigned post. This causes some ants to notice enemies before others, which leads to only half your battallion attacking. That’s a bit… meh.
- I wish there was a ‘patrol’ option to secure a whole resource gathering caravan rather than having to manually move the military where it’s needed along the road.

I enjoyed parts of Empires of the Undergrowth quite a bit, especially the atmosphere, swarm behavior, and constant activity on screen. Watching hundreds of ants move, defend, gather food, and overwhelm enemies is genuinely impressive and makes the colony feel alive in a way many strategy games don’t.

That said, I ended up rating it lower because I was hoping for more of a true long-term colony simulation and less of a mission-based RTS. The game is much more scenario/combat focused than I expected, and while the ants feel believable as a swarm, the colony itself never became something I felt deeply attached to.

The biggest issue for me was that larger battles eventually became very cluttered and chaotic. Huge ant swarms crashing into each other looks cool at first, but over time it became difficult to read strategically and often felt more like visual noise than satisfying tactical gameplay.

I was also disappointed that the Formicarium progression felt strangely disconnected from the actual missions. I kept expecting my colony development there to have a bigger impact on the campaign, but it often felt more like a separate side system than a true evolving ant civilization.

Honestly, I also got the impression that the game was developed over such a long period of time that it slowly lost focus. It feels like a lot of ideas and systems were added because they sounded interesting individually, even when they didn’t always fit together into a cohesive long-term experience.

Still a very unique and well-made game — just not quite the “living ant civilization sim” I was personally hoping for.

This game is incredible. Its a strategy game and documentary rolled into one. You play mostly as ants, but you occasionally get to play as Termites, Spiders, and Beetles. There are a wide variety of creative extra levels and even a custom game mode with near infinite replayability in addition to the 11 documentary story missions and 5 experiments that make up the story mode. Each level is perfectly designed, except for perhaps the first level (New Home). It feels a bit bland in comparison to every other level, but that's ok since its basically a tutorial. The game also has lots of customizable difficulty options. The custom game mode has near perfect costumizable difficulty, and then each level has 5 difficulty settings: Easy, Medium, Hard, Extreme, and Impossible. Impossible is a nightmare. Even though I've got over 300 hours on this game, I've still not beaten every story mode level on Impossible (I've beaten every experiement, New Home, Subjugation, Rising Tide, Triage, and Last Mound Standing on Impossible). There is also a challenge mode available for each documentary level, which adds a critter that will make your rise to power more difficult. 
While the base game is incredible and one of the best games I have ever played, the DLC was not very good. Its a pretty good case of "you get what you pay for." Its 5 dollars, so I don't feel bad about buying it, but all that's in the DLC is you can play as Exploding ants and Exploding Termites, which are funny to use but not particularly good. You get two extra levels, but they're both just story mode levels with your exploding colony added. There is also no new narration, which was one of the coolest parts of the base game. The DLC is ok, and having new colonies for freeplay is always fun, but I would ultimately say that unless you're really really into the game, the DLC isn't a must buy.

The setting is refreshing, but not complicated. Ant enthusiasts & laid-back RTS-players will love this.

Hardcore RTS players however, will find the game to be inconsistent at MAX difficulty. Some missions are simple breeze, with side objectives being very simple. Other missions will be extremely brutal, where unless the stars align, there's ZERO chance of winning the mission. 

This frustrating yo-yo effect on actual difficulty shows that either not enough people efficiently tested the game at max difficulty, OR the devs didn't properly consider the reports given.

Overall, if you're a casual, you'll enjoy.
If you're a hardcore player, I'd suggest looking elsewhere.
